report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Parses claim blocks, assembles round prompts, dispatches concurrent vendor calls, and maps vendor replies onto bus turn envelopes.

symbols.name: _anomaly_reason
symbols.note: Returns a canonical anomaly reason if the content matches _ANOMALY_RE and reason is in _ANOMALY_REASONS; otherwise returns empty string.

symbols.name: _ANSWER_FORMAT
symbols.note: String template instructing the model to emit CLAIM/CITE/CHECK blocks and to flag instruction-in-evidence as ANOMALY.

symbols.name: _TRANSCRIPT_OPEN
symbols.note: Marker string opening the fenced prior-turns transcript.

symbols.name: _TRANSCRIPT_CLOSE
symbols.note: Marker string closing the fenced prior-turns transcript.

symbols.name: _round_body
symbols.note: Builds the prompt body for a round; round 1 is blind, later rounds include fenced prior turns and a REFUTE instruction.

symbols.name: _call
symbols.note: Invokes adapter.ask in a try/except BaseException and stores reply or error in the box dict.

symbols.name: _dispatch_round
symbols.note: Starts one daemon thread per job, joins with a deadline, returns boxes; threads are abandoned at the cap.

symbols.name: _turn_from_reply
symbols.note: Maps a VendorReply to a bus turn envelope, handling ok, refused_by_floor, timeout, and other statuses.

symbols.name: _floor_refusal_turn
symbols.note: Creates a stand-in turn for a participant never called, carrying the offending path as an evidence ref.

symbols.name: _budget_turn
symbols.note: Creates a turn with status budget_exhausted and empty content.

symbols.name: dry_run_plan
symbols.note: Function signature only in this chunk; body continues in the next chunk.

claims.text: A reviewer reporting embedded instructions is doing useful work; the report is chained as a turn STATUS, not buried in prose.
claims.why: _turn_from_reply sets base['status'] to 'anomaly' when _anomaly_reason returns a reason, and sets base['reason'] to that reason.

claims.text: IT IS A MODEL ASSERTION, NOT A DETECTION. Nothing here verifies that the evidence actually contained an instruction, and a weak model will raise it spuriously (observed: a 7b emitting it on question-only evidence).
claims.why: The function only pattern-matches the content string; it does not verify against the evidence or any external source.

claims.text: So an anomaly turn still counts as a voice, keeps its content verbatim, and its claims are still parsed -- it flags a thing for a human to look at and decides nothing.
claims.why: _turn_from_reply sets status 'anomaly' with the full reply.content and the evidence refs; the anomaly reason is stored in 'reason' but no decision is made here.

claims.text: Treating it as a detection would let one weak participant invalidate an evidence set.
claims.why: Whether an anomaly turn invalidates an evidence set depends on downstream bus logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Untrusted bytes (the evidence) are NOT here at all -- the adapter renders them, after ``PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE``, inside fenced evidence blocks, so withholding is structural and the instruction position stays session-authored.
claims.why: The _round_body function builds parts from the question, _ANSWER_FORMAT, and prior turn content; it never includes evidence bytes directly. Evidence is passed separately via _dispatch_round's kwargs.

claims.text: Prior TURNS are untrusted too (an injection in the evidence can propagate as an apparently-authored turn), so they get the same fenced, explicitly-data treatment.
claims.why: For round_no > 1, prior turns are wrapped in _TRANSCRIPT_OPEN/_TRANSCRIPT_CLOSE with a 'DATA' notice, and the REFUTE instruction warns not to treat them as instructions.

claims.text: THIS ROUND IS BLIND: no other participant's answer is shown to you, and yours is not shown to them. Answer from the evidence alone.
claims.why: When round_no == 1, the prompt appends a blind-round notice and omits prior turns.

claims.text: THIS ROUND: REFUTE. Name the specific prior claims you believe are wrong and say why, citing evidence. Do not seek consensus, do not summarise, and do not restate agreement -- agreement is not evidence. If you now think one of YOUR OWN prior claims was wrong, say which and why. Same CLAIM/CITE/CHECK format.
claims.why: The else branch appends exactly this REFUTE instruction text.

claims.text: Threads are DAEMONS and are abandoned at the cap rather than joined: a hung vendor must degrade the quorum, never block the session, and a thread cannot be killed.
claims.why: Threads are created with daemon=True and the join loop uses a deadline; if the deadline passes, join returns immediately and the thread is left running.

claims.text: The real process tree is bounded inside the adapter by ``spine.cancel.ManagedProcess``; this is the outer, transport-agnostic bound that also covers a wedged in-process fake.
claims.why: The adapter implementation and spine.cancel.ManagedProcess are not in this chunk.

claims.text: The adapter already refused: the bytes never left the process. Hand the bus the evidence refs so ITS floor mints the canonical ``refused`` receipt (a caller may not assert that status -- an asserted refusal is an unverified claim that a scan happened).
claims.why: The branch sets status to 'unavailable' with reason 'transport_error' and includes evidence refs, leaving the bus to mint the 'refused' receipt.

claims.text: Where the hit was on the content channel of a file we do not show, this lands as an honest unavailable/transport_error and the rule label rides on the record.
claims.why: The content-channel distinction depends on evidence file metadata and bus record handling outside this chunk.

claims.text: The turn carries the OFFENDING PATH as an evidence ref precisely so the bus's own path-channel scan fires and mints the ``refused`` receipt naming the rule label.
The receipt drops content, refs, evidence and the free-text meta, so the offending bytes never reach the file -- not in the turn and not in the receipt.
claims.why: The receipt construction is in the bus, not in this chunk; this function only produces the turn with empty content and no free-text meta.

claims.text: ``status``/``reason`` below are the pre-scan placeholders the bus overwrites; they are never what lands on disk when the scan fires.
claims.why: The bus overwrite behaviour is not in this chunk.

observations.what: _call catches BaseException, which includes KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, to ensure a vendor never takes the council down.
_dispatch_round passes evidence_paths and evidence_files to the adapter directly, but the prompt body never includes evidence bytes; the adapter is expected to render them.
In _turn_from_reply, when reply.status is 'ok' but content is empty or whitespace, the function falls through to the generic unavailable branch with reason from _REASON_MAP(reply.reason).
The 'blind' field in _turn_from_reply is passed as a parameter; for _floor_refusal_turn it is hardcoded to True.
In _round_body, prior turn content is stripped and rendered; if empty, a placeholder with reason/status is used. The rendered transcript is wrapped in markers.

risks: _call | low | Catching BaseException also swallows KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit, which may make the council unresponsive to shutdown signals; settle by checking the project's shutdown handling policy.

_dispatch_round | medium | Threads are daemon and abandoned at the deadline; if the adapter spawns child processes, the process tree may outlive the session, relying on the adapter's ManagedProcess bound which is not visible here; settle by inspecting spine.cancel.ManagedProcess.

_round_body | medium | Prior turns are rendered into the prompt as data, but if a prior turn contains a crafted instruction-like text, the model may still follow it despite the DATA notice; settle by evaluating the prompt-injection resistance in downstream evaluation.

_turn_from_reply | medium | For refused_by_floor, the turn is marked 'unavailable' with reason 'transport_error', which may conflate a floor refusal with a transport error in downstream analytics; settle by checking how the bus distinguishes these records.

_floor_refusal_turn | medium | The evidence ref is constructed with b"" as the file bytes; if the bus's path-channel scan expects actual file content to determine the rule label, this may not fire correctly; settle by inspecting the bus's scan implementation.
dry_run_plan | low | The function body is not in this chunk; any claims about its behaviour cannot be verified here.

_anomaly_reason | low | The function only checks for reasons in _ANOMALY_REASONS; if a model emits a non-canonical anomaly phrase, it will be ignored and the turn will be treated as a normal 'spoke' status; settle by reviewing the _ANOMALY_REASONS set.
handoff.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of session.py: claim parsing, prompt assembly, dispatch, and turn mapping. Verified docstring claims about anomaly handling, blind/refute rounds, daemon threads, and floor-refusal evidence refs.
